transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-06-10
Time: 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Hayes (Redwood AE), Priya Kapoor (Redwood SE), Alex Moreno (CISO, Suncrest), Tina Wu (Cloud Architect), Marcus Lee (SRE)

Summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Weekly POC security/compliance sync. Discussed SSO/SAML integration progress, audit log export options, data retention and encryption/KMS, SOC2 evidence request, and next steps for an on-prem benchmark. Agreed to share SOC2 and penetration test docs, prepare SAML metadata, enable temporary audit log export to customer S3, and schedule full throughput test next week.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining on time. quick check, is this still a good 45?
[00:05] Alex: yup that's perfect. we've got the CISO slot free for the first 20.
[00:09] Jordan: great, i'll run through the security items first and then priya will cover the bench plan.
[00:15] Priya: hi all, thanks. we want to make sure SSO and audit logging meet Suncrest requirements before we start load.
[00:21] Tina: quick note, tina here — we've got strict retention and e-discovery rules, so retention needs to be configurable per-tenant, and we need proof of deletion.
[00:30] Jordan: totally understood. action item for us is a clear data retention policy doc. we'll also include the KMS/HSM integration notes.
[00:36] Marcus: one more from infra — we need to ensure audit logs can be exported to our S3 in near real-time, and we want immutable logs with object-lock if possible.
[00:44] Priya: we can wire up audit log export via S3 or syslog. the current POC setup supports S3 export; we can enable object-lock if you provide the bucket policy and ARN.
[00:55] Alex: can you confirm what events are logged? admin actions, API keys, inference payloads?
[01:02] Jordan: good question — by default we log admin actions, auth events, model deployments, and error traces. inference payloads are redacted by default in hosted unless you opt-in. we'll send a full schema.
[01:14] Tina: ok; for our regulator we can't have plaintext customer PII in logs. need to see the redaction approach.
[01:20] Priya: right — PII redaction is handled at ingestion: we can mask tokens and we also support client-side tokenization if you want end-to-end. small caveat, it changes debugging fidelity.
[01:33] Marcus: about SSO — we've tried the quick test with the metadata you sent, but our IdP errors out on the audience. it says 'invalid-aud'.
[01:41] Jordan: hmm, that's likely the ACS URL mismatch — priya, do we have the expected audience string?
[01:45] Priya: yes, for the POC environment the SP entity is urn:redwood:poc:suncrest, but production will be different. i'll attach the sample metadata.
[01:53] Alex: production must support SAML 2.0 with signed assertions and attribute mapping for email + employee_id. also need SCIM for user provisioning ideally.
[02:03] Jordan: we support SAML 2.0 signed assertions and have SCIM provisioning as an optional integration for Dedicated and Private deployments. for hosted we can enable SCIM for enterprise accounts.
[02:12] Tina: any blockers around SAML certificate rotation? we need to rotate certs without downtime.
[02:18] Priya: certificate rollover is zero-downtime if you upload both old and new certs in metadata. we'll document exact steps in the SSO guide.
[02:26] Marcus: great. on SOC2 — we need your Type II report and the most recent pen-test summary before we can move forward with the next internal review.
[02:34] Jordan: absolutely. i'll send SOC2 Type II and pen-test summaries after the call. note some redactions in pen-test report for public consumption, but we can provide full evidence under NDA.
[02:46] Alex: NDA is already in place per procurement. will you include the control matrix mapping to our requirements?
[02:52] Jordan: we can include the control matrix. i'll map the relevant controls for encryption at rest, in transit, RBAC, and logging.
[02:59] Tina: about encryption: we want KMS integration and allow customer-managed keys for Dedicated/private. how does Redwood support that?
[03:07] Priya: for Dedicated and Private, you can bring your keys via AWS KMS or external HSM; for hosted, we offer customer-managed keys for enterprise tenants — there's an onboarding flow. we'll include the KMS guide.
[03:19] Marcus: retention scoping — the compliance team wants 7 years for certain records; is that feasible?
[03:25] Jordan: technically yes, but we need to align on storage costs and retention tiers. for the POC we can set retention to 90 days, and if longer-term is required we can propose cold storage.
[03:36] Alex: 90 is fine for the pilot as long as we get confirmation of the deletion workflow and auditable proof.
[03:42] Priya: we can produce deletion proof via audit events and object lifecycle hooks; we'll note the exact export fields in the doc.
[03:50] Jordan: ok moving to audit log detail — priya, can you run through what the log schema has?
[03:55] Priya: sure. high level: timestamp, actor_id, action, resource_id, outcome, request_id. optional payload contains metadata but not full inference text unless explicitly enabled. again, we'll share the full schema.
[04:08] Tina: please make sure request_id ties to the trace id in your traces so we can correlate with our APM.
[04:14] Priya: yes we emit trace_id and span info if tracing is enabled; can be pushed to third-party tracing or included in logs.
[04:22] Marcus: next, legal asked about data residency — we need to make sure logs and telemetry stay in eu-west-1 for eu customers. can redwood pin regions for their tenant?
[04:31] Jordan: yes, we support region pinning. for Dedicated we can provision in eu-west-1; hosted accounts can choose region for data residency. we'll document the region controls.
[04:40] Alex: are there any known issues with your runtime that affect audit granularity or cause missing events under high load?
[04:47] Priya: we do durable write queues for logs — in extreme load we batch but never drop events; there was one edge case last year which we patched where debug logs could be delayed, but not dropped. we'll include the incident summary in the SOC2 appendix.
[05:00] Marcus: ok. now on to the on-prem benchmark plan — priya?
[05:03] Priya: plan is to run a 1k rps sim for 30 minutes against a dedicated pool simulating your steady state, with KV cache warmup and realistic prompt distribution. we want to validate latency SLOs and memory pressure.
[05:17] Tina: will we be able to run these in our VPC? we'd prefer a Private deployment for that test but can do on-prem if needed.
[05:24] Jordan: for this bench we propose either Redwood Private in your VPC or an on-prem test kit. earlier you said VPC peering was acceptable?
[05:31] Tina: yes VPC peering is fine, but we need the network ports and trunk details.
[05:35] Priya: i'll send the network pre-reqs doc. for peering we require specific ports and MTU settings; it's standard.
[05:42] Marcus: what about metrics export? we need Prometheus metrics and Grafana dashboards.
[05:46] Priya: we expose Prometheus endpoints and can ship dashboards; for Private you get direct scrape. for hosted we can forward metrics to your metrics endpoint or Grafana Cloud.
[05:56] Alex: security question — do you provide RBAC with least privilege roles and audit of role changes?
[06:02] Jordan: yes RBAC with admin, ops, observer roles; all role changes are logged and we can show the audit trail.
[06:08] Tina: is there single-tenant isolation at the container/VM level for Dedicated?
[06:13] Priya: Dedicated uses tenant-isolated GPU pools; infra layer is single-tenant for compute and shared control plane unless you do Private full air-gapped.
[06:22] Marcus: could you clarify the difference between Dedicated and Private in terms of KMS and network ownership?
[06:27] Jordan: Dedicated: Redwood manages control plane but you get reserved GPU capacity and can bring KMS keys; Private: you run control plane in your VPC or on-prem, full network and key ownership.
[06:37] Alex: procurement will want to know liability boundaries and support SLAs for Dedicated. can you send a standard contract excerpt?
[06:43] Jordan: yes, we'll share the SLA and support tiers.
[06:47] Priya: quick note on pen tests — our most recent pentest found a low-severity vuln in a third-party lib that was patched; we'll include the remediation timeline.
[06:58] Alex: good. for the audit logs to S3, do you support encryption with our KMS keys?
[07:04] Priya: yes if you provide the KMS key ARN for the bucket we can configure server-side encryption with your key.
[07:11] Marcus: about retention enforcement — if we ask for 7 year retention, do you support tiering to Glacier?
[07:17] Jordan: yes tiering to colder storage is supported; we'll bill separately for long-term storage.
[07:24] Tina: how do you handle legal hold and e-discovery requests? we need the ability to preserve certain records beyond deletion windows.
[07:30] Priya: we have a legal-hold feature; it prevents lifecycle deletion for specified objects and emits audit proofs. we'll include the feature doc.
[07:39] Alex: can I get a sample attestation for encryption keys separation of duties?
[07:44] Jordan: yes, we'll include key management attestation and separation of duties notes.
[07:49] Marcus: one operational question — does Redwood store raw inference payloads in any backups?
[07:55] Priya: backups do not include raw inference payloads unless explicitly enabled. by default we snapshot model artifacts and metadata only. we'll call that out.
[08:03] Alex: ok that helps. timeline wise, can you deliver the SOC2 and SAML docs by tomorrow?
[08:09] Jordan: yes i'll share SOC2 and pen-test by EOD tomorrow. priya will follow with SAML metadata.
[08:15] Priya: i'll also attach the network pre-reqs and log schema in the same thread.
[08:20] Tina: and Marcus will try to push sample traffic profile to you by Friday.
[08:24] Marcus: yep aiming for that.
[08:26] Jordan: last bit — pricing for Dedicated pool. i'll send a ballpark today and a formal quote after we firm up the retention and region.
[08:33] Alex: one more compliance ask — do you have ISO27001 certification? it's not a blocker but nice to know.
[08:39] Jordan: currently SOC2 Type II only, ISO in planning for Q4. we'll note that in the package.
[08:47] Priya: also want to flag that if you need endpoint-level TLS mutual auth for private, we can enable mTLS.
[08:55] Tina: good to know.
[08:58] Jordan: ok let's recap next steps — i'll read them out.
[09:02] Jordan: 1) send SOC2 + pen-test, 2) priya send SAML metadata and network pre-reqs, 3) enable audit log export to S3 for trial, 4) schedule on-prem bench 2026-06-17, 5) confirm retention and e-discovery details.
[09:17] Alex: that matches our expectations.
[09:20] Jordan: any other open items?
[09:22] Tina: just one: can you provide a short runbook for emergency key rotation?
[09:26] Priya: yes we'll include a runbook snippet.
[09:29] Jordan: great. thanks everyone. we'll follow up in threads.
[09:33] Alex: thanks all.
[09:35] End of recording.

Notes on transcription: occasional speaker overlaps and minor mis-hearings; some product names may differ slightly from internal docs (e.g., 'Dedicated pool' vs 'Reserved capacity').
